rows.reflection: The first v14 x2 status was not wrong; it was an honest early snapshot before delayed CLI completion.
Delayed completion is exactly what a no-rush watcher is built to respect.
A superseding receipt is better than rewriting the initial open-gap evidence.
The one-line stdin hardening is valuable even when Codex still logs a generic stdin-read line.
The app lanes continue to be reliable through existing local-server routes.
CLI lane final markers should be treated as delayed evidence, not instant pass/fail signals.
Marker review must distinguish hygiene words from actual sensitive material.
Hash-only publication is the right default for sibling final messages.
The five-lane cadence is now a living practice rather than a statement in one skill file.
x3 is justified when the prior x-session reveals compaction and detector work, not merely because more output is possible.
Source drift keeps pulling THOS toward containment, observability, and evidence discipline.
Every impressive infrastructure source still points back to boring operational truth: logs, states, hashes, and boundaries.
Multi-agent systems can be both more capable and more fragile; topology is a safety variable.
The v14 x2 closeout should reward patience rather than relaunching.
A concise status board is now more valuable than another separate watcher.
Loader drift should be detected before repair, especially after plugin-cache updates.
Command-index repair should surface affordances, not invent authority.
v54/v55 handoff surfacing should be an index, not a raw archive transfer.
Publication guard wording should avoid triggering its own scans when possible.
The x2 arc shows why early receipts and late receipts both matter.
The local Windows ecosystem is moving toward agent containment; THOS should mirror that with explicit local boundaries.
Connector read access must never become assumed write permission.
The safest multi-agent family is one that can pause a lane without losing the whole run.
The next status board should make superseded receipts obvious to future readers.
A good roadmap tells each lane what evidence would prove its task.
THOS should favor small reusable detectors over large one-off repairs.
GMUT can remain inspirational while empirical gates stay explicitly open.
Delayed Arby completion with a marker review was a useful stress test for publication hygiene.
The strongest next move is not bigger orchestration; it is clearer orchestration.
v14 x3 should turn v14 x2 lessons into compact operator tools and sharper closeout criteria.
